messages:
sam: Heads up, noticed a spike in corrected ECC on several us-west nodes starting ~10:15. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/board/gpu-ecc (chart shows cluster mean jumping x6) :eyes:

nina: saw that too, any Xid churn or job failures?

sam: Xid 13 count up a bit but most are corrected ECC. No immediate pod crashes yet. Node IDs: ip-10-2-34-12, ip-10-2-34-18 (both p4d-like).

alex: can you paste the raw query? want to check per-gpu rate vs per-node aggregate.

sam: here's the alert expr we used: 
```
sum by(gpu_serial) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m])) / 5m > 0.2
```
That threshold caught a bunch of cards.

leo: 0.2 corrected ECC/s = ~12/hr which is noisy if a single misbehaving card shows up. We should differentiate sustained vs burst.

nina: agree. proposal: two-tier detection -> (1) burst spike: 5+ corrected events in 5m, mark for temp fencing; (2) sustained elevated rate > 10/hr for 30m -> auto-drain candidate. Also uncorrectable ECC or Xid critical codes auto-drain immediately.

sam: +1 but we need to avoid cascading drains during a fleet-wide transient (e.g., driver release). Need to correlate with rollout tags and kernel dmesg.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: deployment:gpu-drivers tagged at 1796123200 in us-west-1 -> 40% nodes.

alex: if driver rollout coincidence, we should be conservative: add a suppression window when rollout tag present and only escalate to manual triage unless uncorrectable/Xid fatal.

leo: suggestion for scoring: score = w1*(corrected_rate_zscore) + w2*(xid_rate) + w3*(uncorrectable_count). If score > 7 -> auto-drain; 4-7 -> notify and soft-fence; <4 -> log. We can compute per-GPU and per-node.

sam: love the scoring idea. what weights? propose w1=1, w2=2, w3=5. Uncorrectable should basically force action.

nina: implementable but need enrichment: gpu_serial, host_label, rack, fitted_age, replacement history. We want to avoid re-draining recently repaired GPUs.

leo: add a decay to past incidents: reduce score if last replacement < 72h.

alex: playbook draft for when score >7 (auto-drain path):
```
1) Mark node unschedulable (kubectl cordon)
2) Trigger graceful drain with arg --delete-local-data --force for lowest-impact pods
3) Re-route new requests away via routing tag (dedicated pool -> spare pool)
4) Create incident ticket with prefilled template (include gpu_serial, host, XR diagnostics)
5) Kick diag job: run nvbugdump.sh + collect dmesg/cuda logs -> upload to s3://redwood/gpu-failures/<node>/
6) If uncorrectable or Xid fatal present, put node into hardware replace queue
```

nina: for 'soft-fence' (score 4-7) do: increase monitoring resolution (1m), apply kube taint no-schedule for non-critical pools, notify oncall channel, block auto-replace.

sre-oncall: one operational note: we need a circuit-breaker to avoid mass-drain during noisy events. Suggested global cap: auto-drain limited to 3 nodes per region per hour unless manually overridden.

sam: yep cap is necessary. also add cooldown per-host: only one auto-drain in 24h unless uncorrectable returned.

ops-bot: added label:gpu-serial to logs ingestion. will start piping serial metadata into grafana metrics in ~20m.

leo: good — that enables hotspot detection. Also want to enrich stackdriver alerts with `recent_replacements` and `last_kernel_update` fields.

alex: rollout plan for the feature:
- week 1: metric enrichment + alert refinement (no auto actions)
- week 2: soft-fence evaluation + scoring in simulation mode (alerts annotated but no cordon)
- week 3: enable auto-drain behind a feature flag in canary region (us-west-2) limited to dedicated pools and cap enforcement
- week 4: collect metrics, manual review, then wider enable with same caps

nina: we should add a fallback to reduce job retries and surface to devs: when a node is cordoned auto-evict low-priority jobs first. update job scheduling docs.

sam: quick question: what counts as Xid fatal? list?

leo: Xid 13/31 are common cuda driver faults; classify Xid that cause kernel oops or GPU resets as fatal. We'll maintain mapping in infra repo: infra/gpu/xid_classification.md

nina: ops runbook snippet to put in docs channel:
```
When ECC spike detected:
- check deployment tags -> if driver/kernel rollout ongoing, escalate to infra lead
- if uncorrectable or Xid fatal -> immediate cordon and escalate to hw team
- otherwise follow scoring -> soft-fence or auto-drain depending on score
- attach nvbugdump and dmesg to ticket
```

sam: action items assigned:
- @ops-bot: start shipping gpu_serial metadata (in progress)
- @leo: prototype scoring calculator and sim mode (this week)
- @alex: add suppression logic for driver rollouts and global cap enforcement (this week)
- @nina: update runbook + add threshold suggestions to alerts (today)

nina: i'll write the thresholds doc: initial thresholds we agreed: burst = >=5 corrected in 5m; sustained = >= 10/hr over 30m; xid spike = >=3 of Xid fatal in 10m -> immediate action; uncorrectable >0 -> immediate action. will add caveats.

sre-oncall: please add a dashboard panel that shows "auto-drain quota used / hour" so oncall has visibility before thresholds kick.

sam: thanks everyone. i'll loop back after leo's sim runs. :thumbsup:
